resolved_findings.consequence: A slow fsync/publication or scheduling delay can consume lease lifetime and still start a remote job. Post-result refusal does not protect the worker lifetime during execution.
resolved_findings.evidence: Clock-boundary diagnostic advanced wall and monotonic clocks7200s during the actual active-record publication. SSH handler entered; only afterward dispatch_deadline_exceeded refused and state became uncertain. Fixture lease lifetime was1hour.
resolved_findings.fix: Recheck effective time after durable publication and before yielding to SSH. Ensure the actual execution budget plus justified cleanup margin fits the original observation; align actual handler deadline with the admitted absolute window rather than silently restarting a full timeout. Preserve conservative durable state if interruption prevents proving nonlaunch.
resolved_findings.issue: Lease lifetime is checked before durable attempt publication, but SSH starts afterward with a fresh full timeout and no prelaunch lifetime recheck.
resolved_findings.verification: A clock-controlled active-publication delay that exhausts remaining lifetime must invoke no handler. Include a still-valid but insufficient-whole-job case and retain normal drain/retry cases.
